angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 647,001 km at 81.14 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.3247 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 81.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.93 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1710 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract): 647,001 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.02 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1710 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5775 +/- 80 K from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1710 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1710 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1710.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.510, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): spectral type G5 V, from Orell-Miquel et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..96O/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.04 dex, from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.0655, from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): age 1 Gyr, from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): rotation period 21.3 d, from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1710 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.1 km/s, from Espinoza-Retamal et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026ApJ..1005L..15E/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.93 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.951. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
